relations.justification: Formal ontology and biological systematics both face the same tension between a classification that is convenient and one that is true to descent.
Formal ontologies generalise the classification impulse that mathematics applies to its own objects, though the machinery differs.
Persistent identifiers require metadata to resolve to; an identifier with no description is a name for something nobody can find.
Retrieval systems are built on indexing structures that database theory supplies.
Terminology work is controlled-vocabulary work applied to a domain.
Archival description is knowledge organisation applied to aggregates rather than items.
Maps and atlases are the artefacts cartography produces; the reference collection specialises the discipline.
The base units are what the fixed constants define; the constant values are chosen precisely to fix them.
The fixed constants that define the SI are quantum-mechanical quantities; the unit system is defined by the theory.
Definition by fixed physical constants superseded definition by artefact: a prototype could drift and a constant cannot.
Dimensional analysis operates on units; the system of units is constitutive of the method.
Uncertainty is stated in units; a measurement cannot be qualified before it is expressed.
Dimensionless groups and scale-invariant laws are the same insight: behaviour depends on ratios rather than absolute size.
Traceability is comparison against a reference in stated units and dimensions.
Systematic error in measurement and confounding in inference are the same defect: a bias that repetition does not remove.
Reproducibility claims depend on knowing what counts as agreement, which is an uncertainty question before it is a methodological one.
Traceability is a chain to a maintained reference; without the standards bodies the chain terminates in nothing.
Time and frequency standards support distributed computing; ordering across machines rests on a shared clock discipline.
Experimental physics is measurement; units, calibration and uncertainty precede any physical claim.
Recommended constant values support every physical calculation and are the reason results from different laboratories are comparable.
Engineering reference tables derive from the disciplines that measured the properties; the tabulation is the discipline made usable.
A standard operating procedure requires a documentation structure a reader can follow under stress; an SOP organised by system rather than task fails at the moment it is needed.
A checklist exemplifies a deliberately impoverished model — it omits almost everything in order to be executable under load.
Patent searching depends on classification schemes; the international classification is what makes prior art findable.
Preservation of physical records and digital media both require a refresh cycle matched to the medium lifetime; storage without migration is deferred loss.
